title: Pick which robot training save to retrain from
summary: Himanshu Kumar's agent picks where a simulated robot retrains from using a graph of past saves and test results; a graph rule changed its pick, and a regressed result was blocked.
agent_role: The agent queries the training history, compares candidate saved versions, and writes down its choice and reasons before training starts. A fixed test gate and a comparison with the parent version, both set by the developer, decide whether the result ships.
outcome: Author reports that a graph rule he added changed the agent's choice in the final run. The new version still did worse than its parent and was blocked from shipping.
what_they_did: The developer stored every saved version of a simulated robot driving policy in a connected database. Each save was linked to its parent, its test results, its failures and past decisions. An agent uses query tools to find the best save to retrain from. It records why it chose before any training runs. Each save is tested on four suites, 180 test runs in total.
how_it_went: He says the agent first repeated a past failure even after reading about it. So he made the graph enforce a rule against it. In the final run that rule changed the agent's pick. The retrained robot still regressed, and the gate stopped it from shipping.
worth_knowing: Telling the agent about past failures was not enough to stop it repeating them; the rule had to be enforced by the system. The author also treats a version family with no recorded problems as unexamined, not safe.
prompt: Here is my training history: [list of saved model versions, their parent versions, and test results per test suite]. Find which versions passed every test suite under these limits: [pass thresholds]. Flag version families where a child got worse than its parent. Recommend which version I should retrain from and why. List every option you considered with its rank. Write your reasoning down before I start any training, and wait for my approval.

curation.rationale: A detailed, honest account with code and a live demo. An agent uses a connected record of past training runs to choose where a simulated robot should retrain from, and a fixed safety check blocks a result that got worse. It is unusual, though built for a hackathon and quite technical.
